t: Born in Bonn into a musical family with an alcoholic father, Beethoven moved to Vienna in 1792, studied with Haydn and became known first as a piano virtuoso and improviser in the salons of the nobility.

From about 1798 his hearing declined, and in 1802 he wrote the Heiligenstadt Testament, recording thoughts of suicide and his resolution to go on living for his art; he never became totally deaf, but by 1818 he and his visitors were writing their conversations in notebooks.

His last years brought the Missa solemnis, the Ninth Symphony, the Diabelli Variations and the late quartets, alongside a bitter legal contest with his sister-in-law over his nephew Karl, who attempted suicide in 1826.
dyk: Beethoven learned to add but never to divide or multiply, and all his life he multiplied by addition, for instance adding up a column of sixteen sevens rather than working out 16 × 7.
ev: Baptised at St. Remigius in Bonn on 17 December; the date of his birth is not documented
Moves permanently to Vienna in November to study with Joseph Haydn, as news arrives that his father has died
Makes his public debut in Vienna over three days, beginning on 29 March at the Burgtheater, and arranges publication of the three piano trios of Opus 1
Writes the Heiligenstadt Testament at Heiligenstadt, recording his thoughts of suicide because of his growing deafness
The Eroica Symphony premieres in early 1805, and Fidelio, in its first version, opens in November to nearly empty houses
Gives a benefit concert in December that premieres the Fifth and Sixth symphonies, the Fourth Piano Concerto and the Choral Fantasy
The Ninth Symphony, with sections of the Missa solemnis, is first performed on 7 May at the Kärntnertortheater
Dies in Vienna on 26 March; about 10,000 people attend the funeral procession three days later

f.born: Baptised on 17 December 1770 at the Catholic parish of St. Remigius in Bonn; the birth date is not documented, though there is a consensus, with which Beethoven himself agreed, that it was 16 December; son of Johann van Beethoven, a court tenor, and Maria Magdalena Keverich
f.died: 26 March 1827 in Vienna, aged 56, after several months of illness; buried in the Währing cemetery after a funeral procession on 29 March attended by an estimated 10,000 people, and reinterred in 1888 at Vienna's Zentralfriedhof
f.role: Court organist at Bonn under Elector Maximilian Franz; from 1792 a composer and piano virtuoso in Vienna, supported by noble patrons including Prince Lichnowsky, Prince Lobkowitz and Archduke Rudolf; composer in residence at the Theater an der Wien (1803–1804)
f.known: nine symphonies, including the Eroica, the Fifth and the Ninth; piano sonatas, among them the Pathétique, the Moonlight and the Hammerklavier; the string quartets, including the late quartets and the Große Fuge; the opera Fidelio; the Missa solemnis; the Diabelli Variations; composing through progressive deafness
